title: Personal Credit Cards: Combined Credit Line Ceiling Across a Customer's Cards
content:
Credit extended on Personal Credit Cards is measured across every card a customer holds with Piedmont Crescent Bank, not card by card. The measure is the sum of the credit limits on every card of the customer that is pending approval, active or suspended on the day of the decision, with the account under decision counted at the limit requested or newly set. Secured Visa limits are counted in the same way as any other limit.

## Ceiling

- Standard ceiling: 75000.00 USD in combined credit lines.
- For a customer with a Private Client Checking account in active status: 150000.00 USD.

The combined figure may not rise above the applicable ceiling as a result of an approval or a credit limit increase. The test draws only on the bank's records of the customer's card accounts and checking accounts, taken before the action.

## What happens at the ceiling

| Situation | Effect |
|---|---|
| Approval or increase keeps the combined figure within the ceiling | proceeds as requested |
| Approval would push the combined figure above the ceiling | the new limit is cut back to the room left; if that room is smaller than the tier's lowest credit limit, the application is declined |
| Increase would push the combined figure above the ceiling | the increase is cut back to the room left; if no room is left, the increase is declined |
| Decrease | never restricted by the ceiling |

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A customer without Private Client Checking holds cards with limits of 30000.00 USD and 38000.00 USD, a combined 68000.00 USD, and is approved for a tier whose lowest limit is 5000.00 USD. The room left under the 75000.00 USD ceiling is 7000.00 USD, so a requested 10000.00 USD limit is cut back to 7000.00 USD. Had the existing lines totalled 71500.00 USD, the room of 3500.00 USD would sit below the tier's lowest limit and the application would be declined. The same customer, if holding an active Private Client Checking account, would be measured against 150000.00 USD instead.
